top.line: A brief for an independent online English teacher: agents that draft, a teacher who decides, and a policy for every agent.
top.para: She is excellent at teaching and runs everything else by hand. Open-ended agents would send her back to pen and paper, so each of seven agents gets a behaviour policy: none sends email, changes her calendar or refunds a payment. The plumbing is Workspace, Claude, GitHub, a private vault, Stripe and the reading meter. With it, every good explanation becomes a page that earns, and practice fits each student, built on retrieval and spacing.

in-short.line: A great teacher, agents she can trust, policies for each, plumbing once, and time to be creative.
in-short.para: A worked example is in a vault.

teacher.line: Excellent at the lessons; enquiries, bookings, payments and follow-ups all by hand.
teacher.para: The same shape as the site for my brother: valuable work every day, and no system to find people or keep it working.

danger.line: Agents that email students or move lessons would fail once and lose her trust for good.
danger.para: The answer is agents that can only do what she asked, with what holds each line written down as a Boundary, Setting or Expectation.

loop.line: Found, trial booked, lesson, materials, follow-up, practice, next lesson, renewal.
loop.para: Agents draft materials, emails and links; she approves and sends; Google runs the booking; the student practises.

agents.line: Seven agents: tutor, follow-up, scheduler, materials, pipeline, billing, weekly brief.
agents.para: Anthropic documents the Gmail and Calendar connectors as read-only; the design relies on agents not having tools, not on settings the account can change.

setup.line: Workspace Business Starter, Claude, GitHub Pages, her domain, two vaults, Stripe, the meter, a policy per agent.
setup.para: Starter has a single booking page; payments go through Stripe links, with no monthly fee and 1.5% + €0.25 for cards and MB WAY.

paid.line: Lesson packages by link, lesson pages by the reading meter, and products made once and sold many times.
paid.para: Workbooks, company courses, exam sets and licences for schools.

creative.line: Every good explanation published as a page, experiments that explain by moving, practice for each student.
creative.para: Not by learning styles, which the evidence does not support, but on retrieval practice and spacing, which it does.

graph.line: Her teaching as a knowledge graph of concepts, and each student's progress as a projection of it.
graph.para: The worked example has thirteen concepts across three levels; it informs her decisions, it does not make them.

not-replaced.line: The lessons, the judgement and every message to a student stay hers.
not-replaced.para: She stops being the bottleneck, and her best work keeps working after the lesson.

limits.line: The teacher is fictional and the setup not yet done for a real one; some barriers are Expectations.
limits.para: Prices change; the CEFR pages were not checked; GitHub Pages' commercial terms are a judgement.

sources.line: Google, Anthropic, Stripe, GitHub, and the learning research cited.
